Gray LEAVE and bright amber WAIT are readable beside the physical wrist boundary. The crossed grip, leaning posture and suspended shoe express a resisted departure.
The panel contains a large photographic portrait matching the main bob, face and blue garment, plus a small WAIT avatar with the same appearance.
The subject leans toward the trapped arm, looks toward that contact, parts the lips and grips the affected forearm. This supports a directed alarm reading without proving private beliefs.
The dark short bob, fine separated fringe, large dark eyes, small nose and full lips visibly follow the actual reference. This is qualitative appearance resemblance, not verified identity.

Both hands support the sheet and a thumb touches the nearly erased portrait. That thumb belongs to the subject’s left hand at viewer-right, reversing the frozen right-thumb assignment. The gaze is downward to the sheet but its exact fading-portrait target is not fully established.
